title: url_holds_credential reads a password that holds a backslash in the scp form as no credential since the Windows-path fix banned every backslash
goal: kbcommon.url_holds_credential still reads user:password@host:path with a backslash in the password as a credential while a drive-letter or UNC path with an @ in a folder name is none

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbcommon as k;b=chr(92);s='jan:pa'+b+'ss@host:path';print(k.url_holds_credential(s));sys.exit(0 if k.url_holds_credential(s) else 1)

import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbcommon as k
b=chr(92)
cred=k.url_holds_credential('jan:pa'+b+'ss@host:path')
drive=k.url_holds_credential('C:'+b+'Users'+b+'jan@home'+b+'file.txt')
unc=k.url_holds_credential(b+b+'srv'+b+'share'+b+'jan@x'+b+'f')
print(cred,drive,unc);sys.exit(0 if cred and not drive and not unc else 1)

notes: Outbound paths: url_holds_credential is called by kbcommon.py:724, kbroot.py:188 (the url a root registers) and census.py:2942; the change is inside the function in kbcommon.py, so all three read the same narrowed rule. Planted check runs the backslash password (a credential) and the drive-letter and UNC paths with an @ folder name (none).
